label: copy-phase input n (fed-back n, not first copy step)
explanation: Token detector for the letter n being read back in during the copy phase. Fires on essentially every copy-phase step whose input is n (that is, original token recall_idx-1 is n) once recall_idx >= 2, with no false positives on dev. Activation is fairly uniform (median ~0.77 of max) across recall_idx, L, out_tok and in_count. Strongest activations tend to come late in the copy (later positions or n near the end of the original). Near-silent (activation <0.07 of max) when the fed-back n is the first copy-phase input (n at original position 0, recall_idx 1). Never fires on n in the original phase, at the delimiter, or on any other input token.

issues: Test scores reproduce: P=1.0, R=0.983, F1=0.991, mass recall 0.9994, 0 false positives on test.

Every test miss is a weak activation (0.01-0.04 of max) on n as the first copy-phase input (recall_idx 1). That is the documented exception, not a systematic gap. Dropping recall_idx>=2 gives test F1 0.907, which matches the claimed ~0.91.
Original-phase firing is 1 step out of 3.2M and other input tokens give fewer than 10 activations in total, so 'never fires' holds as a near-absolute.

Minor magnitude nuance the explanation leaves out: the 2nd and 3rd n of a run of consecutive fed-back n's is somewhat lower (~0.67-0.83 vs ~0.97 for the run's first n in top examples), and the lowest-quartile examples fall at recall_idx 2 (0.5-0.64). So magnitude is a bit less flat than stated, but this does not affect what the feature fires on.
